# SUTTON PLANNING BOARD

## Meeting Minutes

October 5, 2026

The Chair read the following notice: Pursuant to Governor Healey's directive extending the temporary Open Meeting provisions until June 30, 2027, the Planning Board meeting will be conducted in a HYBRID format and will be recorded. *Any person in attendance making an audio or video recording of this meeting must notify the Chair at this time. *Recordings will be available on the Town's website and YouTube channel. *Please be aware: Participants attending via Zoom will have their video and audio disabled. *If you wish to engage in discussion, raise your hand; if the Chair acknowledges you, you will receive a pop-up message allowing you to unmute yourself. For agenda, YouTube, and Zoom links, please visit www.suttonma.gov.

Present in person: W. Stanhope, W. Talcott, R. Largess Jr., M. Gagan, Dave Mason, Associate (acting as full member)

Present remotely: none

Absent: E. McCallum

Staff: J. Hager, Community Development Director

## Public Hearings

### 354 West Sutton Road – Public Shade Tree & Scenic Roadway Alteration

W. Talcott read the hearing notice as it appeared in The Millbury Sutton Chronicle.

Margaret Bacon of Civil Site engineering was present representing the applicant. The project involves the removal of three public shade trees to install a driveway to the proposed home and maintain adequate sight distance. Additionally, a 20' +/- break will have to be created in the existing stone wall along the right of way/front property line for the driveway. The Board viewed the plan and photographs.

Nick Repetka, Sutton Highway Superintendent and Tree Warden provided written commentary and was also present. He felt all three trees had life left in them and one in particular, a 36" oak, was in good condition. He felt it would be appropriate for the applicant to make a donation to the Town's tree planting and maintenance fund to compensate for the value of public trees being removed.

B. Talcott noted when stones are removed, there should be no re-creation of the remaining stone wall, it should stay in its current form.

The Board reviewed department comments. It was unclear if taxes due had been paid. There were no public comments.

Motion: To grant the scenic roadway alteration allowing the removal of 18' of existing stone wall and removal of three public shade trees to accommodate a driveway with the following conditions: R. Largess Jr.

1. All stones removed are to stay on the subject property.
2. The applicant shall obtain any additional necessary permits (i.e. road opening permit).
3. The applicant shall pay $600.00 to the Town's public shade tree planting and maintenance fund to partially compensate for the value of public shade trees being removed.
4. The tree removal company shall be licensed and properly insured.
5. Contingent on payment of taxes.

2nd: D. Mason

Vote: 5-0-0, D. Mason – aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, W. Stanhope – aye, W. Talcott – aye, M. Gagan – aye

Motion: To close the public hearing, W. Talcott

2nd: M. Gagan

Vote: 5-0-0, D. Mason – aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, W. Stanhope – aye, W. Talcott – aye, M. Gagan – aye

## Action Items

### ANR Plans - 26R Oakhurst Road

Conveyance of land from 38 Oakhurst Road to 26R Oakhurst Road to provide legal frontage and some additional area for this lot in accordance with a variance granted by the ZBA on 9/10.

Motion: To approve the Form A Plan dated 9/25/26 showing reconfiguration of two existing lots including establishing legal frontage for the land at 26R Oakhurst Road. Endorsement of the plan shall be held until 10/6 to ensure no appeal is filed to the related ZBA decision. If an appeal is filed, the applicant agrees to withdraw its Form A application until the appeal is settled. W. Talcott

2nd: R. Largess Jr.

Vote: 5-0-0, D. Mason – aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, W. Stanhope – aye, W. Talcott – aye, M. Gagan – aye

### 16 John Road - As-built Plan Consideration

The Board received a request to continue discussion on this item until their next meeting to allow the applicant time to rectify substantial issues at the site. The Board stressed they expect all, or nearly so, of the issues to be addressed. R. Largess Jr. felt the applicant should provide weekly progress reports.

### UGPG-Truck Traffic Discussion

Mario Giamei of 86 Boston Road was present restating concerns with continued UGPG truck traffic on Boston Road between Providence Road and Route 146. The Unified Parkway definitive subdivision decision contained a condition that once complete, UGPG trucks would not turn left onto Boston Road when exiting this roadway. Matt Piekarski, Director of Development for the Kraft Group was present on behalf of UGPG. He stated their covenant expires in December and they expect to have the road complete in the next week or two. He agreed trucks will not turn left out of Unified Parkway, but he noted the conditions of approval did not apply to trucks departing and returning to UGPG Headquarters at 223 Worcester Providence Turnpike. These trips range from 12-15 trucks per day and may continue to use this stretch of public road. He noted work on building 2 will likely begin in the next 6-12 months so they'll want to keep the site secure, prompting them to keep this private road closed to the general public. However, to meet their obligations to the town they will establish a means for traffic generated along the roadway to utilize the Providence Road access, likely through some type of gating system. They will likely also direct trucks from 38 and 68 Providence Road to utilize this roadway to travel to and from Route 146 at that point. Trucks returning to the Route 146 facility from points east through Grafton may choose to bypass the difficult turn at Boston Road and instead use Unified Parkway to travel west to Route 146, but this can't be guaranteed. R. Largess Jr. asked if there was a physical way to keep trucks from turning left. M. Piekarski stated likely not as the intersection is complete and a configuration that still allows employees and visitors to turn left would be difficult. W. Talcott asked at what point Providence Road would fully open. Mr. Piekarski said not for the foreseeable future but it depends on who the Lot 1 user. Mr. Giamei stated the road should be public, but said he appreciated the update and would appreciate all consideration UGPG can give to limiting truck use on this denser residential stretch of Boston Road. He stated he also appreciated UGPG addressing his concerns with lighting at 40 Unified Parkway.

### Ballot Question 7-Small Lots

J. Hager noted this discussion is meant to call Sutton citizens' attention to the initiative, and provide some factual information, with caveats, for decision they may make at the November election. While this ballot initiative and is not specific to Sutton, it has potential consequences on development in all Massachusetts communities. In accordance with the language of the ballot question requiring 1) availability of both water and sewer, 2) a minimum of 50' frontage, and 3) a minimum area of 5,000 s.f., J. Hager asked the GIS department at CMRPC to provide an analysis of how many additional lots could be created in Sutton. It would be very difficult to account for whether the location of current structures would allow such divisions, and whether resulting lots could meet the 60% upland, coverage, and setback requirements, or if owners would create new roadways to create more lots. Further, it is impossible to know whether current or future land owners would even choose to exercise this option, so the number we will receive is likely conservative. It was noted one size fits all is generally not a good planning/growth strategy. Regardless, hopefully discussion raises awareness and provides at least some knowledge base to assist voters at November's election.

### Amazon Drone Delivery

Again, in an attempt to raise Sutton residents' awareness, J. Hager has provided a copy of the power point presentation from an information session by Amazon. The proposed request in Westborough to allow drone delivery infrastructure and use at this location would voluntarily serve customers but potentially effect properties over a 7.5-mile radius from the Westborough facility. This includes a small portion of NE Sutton in the vicinity of Blackstone Street and Chase Road. While there are eventually potential benefits in terms of reduction in on road delivery impacts, there are many questions about trade off impacts. Questions persist about what can be seen or heard of the roughly 5' square drones from the typical 200-400' flight path as well as noise frequency and duration, including more direct impacts adjacent to individual delivery locations. The FAA has reportedly approved this use, but the FAA does not own US air space, they regulate navigable airspace. Until now it has been widely accepted that Federal authority pre-empts local restrictions on aircraft, including that local jurisdictions cannot set altitude limits or no fly zones without FAA coordination. But drones are a slightly different animal. Adding to the confusion is the 1946 Supreme Court decision, US v. Causby, that established that landowners hold rights to the lower airspace directly above their property sufficient to enable "full enjoyment" of it. Therefore, many questions have arisen about an individual's or a community's rights to prohibit drone use over public and/or private property. R. Largess Jr. asked if private drone users will be given the same autonomy as commercial users to fly over private and public property. The majority of the Board felt it would be good to know what other more impacted communities have found out about the legality of regulation of the use.
